card:hook: An eighteen hundred pound payment. The invoice matches it to the penny. Should this alert be closed?
card:title: Screening desk reads each alert the way a good analyst does, and shows its working.
1 · Read the case: Step one. It reads the customer, and what they told the bank to expect.
2 · Read the alert: Step two. The alert: the payee matched an entry on the bank's internal list.
3 · Read the policy: Step three. This bank's own policy, and its limits.
4 · Match the documents to the money: Step four. Match the documents to the money. The invoice explains the payment.
5 · Look for signs of crime: Step five. Look for signs of crime. The register shows the listed director still owned sixty percent on the day the money moved.
6 · Test each alert: Step six. Test each alert. This one is not explained.
7 · Decide: ESCALATE, and never contact: Step seven. Decide. It escalates, and drafts the referral, without contacting the customer.
Most alerts do close: the gift letter ma: Most alerts do close. Here, a gift letter matches the deposit on donor, amount and date.
The same desk, inside a chat bot, throug: And the same desk works inside a chat bot, through its connector.
A new alert: escalated, referral drafted: A new alert lands. It escalates, drafts the referral, and leaves the customer alone.
Asked why, it answers from the case file: Asked why, it answers from the case file. The rules decide. The bot explains.
card:close: Twenty-eight checks that run as code. Four thousand alerts in under three seconds, identical on every run. And nothing closes unless the evidence explains it.
